sentences.quote: Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group Inc. named Toru Nakashima as chief executive officer, turning to an experienced insider to lead Japan's second-largest bank following the death of his predecessor.
sentences.text: Toru Nakashima has been president and group chief executive officer of Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group since December 1, 2023, taking the role days after the sudden death of his predecessor Jun Ohta; he had been serving as interim chief and was an experienced insider at Japan's second-largest bank.

Born in 1963 in Aichi Prefecture, he graduated from the University of Tokyo's engineering faculty in 1986 and joined Sumitomo Bank, later holding posts including head of the retail banking and corporate planning departments before becoming group CFO and CSO in 2019 and deputy president in 2023.
He currently serves as director and president, representative executive officer, and group CEO of the holding company.
He has also served as a director of Jefferies Financial Group since August 2024.

sentences.text: Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group delivered record FY2025 results, with net income of 1.583 trillion yen and EPS of 412 yen, both record highs, and ROE above 10%, meeting the targets of its previous medium-term plan.

Its new three-year plan backcasts from a medium- to long-term goal, aiming to lift net income to 2 trillion yen and reach ROTE of 13% by FY2028 through expense control and better RORA, en route to 15% ROTE and net income in the mid-2 trillion yen range.
Earnings are supported by domestic rate normalization, as profit rose sharply from domestic businesses on Bank of Japan rate hikes while Olive strengthened the deposit and payment customer base.
Shareholder returns are rising, with annual dividends of 157 yen per share, a 38% payout ratio, and a buyback of up to 180 billion yen, all to be cancelled.
